title: The Eleven-Day Delay

narrative.text: Vyktor delivers this morning's intelligence briefing himself — a small, significant gesture, because there is no BNI director to deliver it. He has the manner of a man presenting a document he would rather not have seen.

Arcturian satellite imagery — shared with us this morning, through Ambassador Cole's office, as a 'courtesy.' It shows a Tyvaren armored brigade that has repositioned 40 kilometers closer to the Gravenmark Pass. Standard assessment puts that as a 3-day movement. It was completed 11 days ago.

We missed an armored brigade repositioning forty kilometers closer to the Gravenmark Pass. The movement was completed eleven days ago. Our border observation posts cover the passes themselves — not the assembly areas forty kilometers to the rear. The BNI signals station at Watchtower Three would have intercepted the communications traffic from that repositioning within forty-eight hours. That station is now decommissioned. The Chancellor dissolved the agency that provided warning. The gap is not theoretical. It is eleven days wide and widening.

Cole waited eleven days. That was deliberate. He is showing me the size of the gap — not to help me, but to demonstrate that I need him. The Arcturian offer of a formal intelligence partnership has been sitting on Vyktor's desk for three weeks. I did not think I could accept it without compromising our independence. I am reconsidering the definition of independence.

Cole's office has already followed up this morning. They describe the sharing as evidence of 'the deep partnership our nations could formalize.' The word 'could' is doing a great deal of work. Ambassador Cole is available to meet this afternoon if you wish to discuss the terms.

monologue: Eleven days. Cole waited eleven days to share the satellite imagery — not to help us, to demonstrate the size of the gap. The Arcturian partnership has been sitting on Vyktor's desk for three weeks because I thought independence meant refusing foreign intelligence. Independence means being able to see. Right now we can't. Whether I build our own eyes or borrow someone else's — and whether borrowing means owing.

choices.text: "Schedule the meeting with Cole. We negotiate a formal intelligence-sharing framework — reciprocal access, not dependency. I want terms that give us their satellite coverage and they get our border observation data. No military basing rights, no political alignment requirements in the agreement itself. If he wants those conversations, they happen separately."

"We begin rebuilding. Not the BNI — something smaller, civilian, with a judicial warrant requirement from day one. I want a draft charter on my desk in two weeks. Dusek, in the interim, I am authorizing you to reactivate the Watchtower Three signals station under direct military command — no civilian intelligence function, purely border monitoring. We build our own eyes before we borrow someone else's."

reactions.text: I will adjust the readiness posture.

choices.text: "Increase border patrol frequency at Gravenmark by fifty percent. I want visual confirmation of that brigade's position within forty-eight hours from our own observers. We cannot afford formal intelligence structures right now. We can afford more boots and more eyes at the pass. Dusek, the overtime cost comes from the contingency fund — don't run it through the standard budget line."

reactions.text: She does not speak. She is filing it away.
His expression does not change. His pen moves anyway.
